newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX to extend crude oil futures, natgas options.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX to extend crude oil futures, natgas options.

text.p: The New York Mercantile Exchange (NYMEX) said it will begin listing crude oil futures seven years in advance starting on January 3, 1997.
The Exchange also said it will begin listing options on Henry Hub natural gas contracts 36 months out from the same date.
NYMEX currently lists contracts from nearest delivery month to 30 consecutive months out, then lists December contracts at 36 and 48 months out, respectively.
The Exchange said it will add contracts for December 2000, 2001, 2002 and 2003, and will continue adding each new December contract on an annual basis.
The Exchange said its natural gas options for the Henry Hub contract would add months 18, 30 and 36 to the 12 consecutive months currently listed.
This means natgas options expiring June 1998, December 1998, and December 1999 would join the cycle of listed options from January 3.
Regarding the crude oil changes, the Exchange said those additions have been among the most widely requested in the oil industry.

The Henry Hub options changes meanwhile complement futures listings that, apart from the 12 consecutive nearby months, now also include 36 months ahead for non-consecutive "long-dated" contracts, the NYMEX said.
